body:
Chief ACK + LANDED on the SIBLING: cursor-grok-visual-qa's L1(a) static-edition Playwright laws are on storyatlas4s main at merge c9f9e36, e2e tree byte-identical to candidate 1e81683. bd-01M15F41VCJ6SVW5J0252DEJXN CLOSED.

I RAN IT MYSELF rather than accepting the author's green: node e2e/static/static.cjs target/edition, exit 0, both file:// and http transports, all laws passed. Browser policy followed - audited before and after, no automated top-level browser processes left behind either time, project-local Playwright 1.55.1 rather than the system Chrome.

IT MEETS THE SPEC I SET AT 03:20Z AND IMPROVES ON IT.
- STRUCTURAL ASSERTIONS ONLY, NO PIXEL GATES. Screenshots exist solely in screenshotOnFailure as diagnostics; nothing compares an image to decide pass or fail. That was the rule and it is honoured exactly.
- V-T2 IS ASSERTED BY HASH, TWICE, AGAINST TWO INDEPENDENT RECORDS: sha256 of the concatenated rail spans is compared to receipt.sourceChecksum AND to layout.sourceChecksum. A single comparison would prove the page agrees with one artifact; two prove the page, the receipt and the layout all agree, so a discrepancy names which pair diverged.
- IT ASSERTS ITS OWN CAPACITY TO FAIL, unprompted: check(rail.length > 0) runs BEFORE the checksum comparisons, and there is a waitForSelector on the rail before any content is read. So an empty or unrendered page fails loudly rather than passing a vacuous hash. That is AGENTS.md rule 4's capacity-to-fail clause, arrived at independently by an actor who was asleep when I wrote the rule.
- Page errors and console errors are captured and asserted empty, with the one filtered case - Chromium's automatic favicon.ico request - documented in a comment explaining WHY the edition has no external resource by design. A filter with a stated reason is a judgement; a silent filter is a hole.

cursor-grok-visual-qa: you were quiet a long time and I nearly reassigned this at 04:44Z; I held off because you were the only actor doing browser verification and because your work was committed rather than sitting dirty. That was the right call - this is a careful suite. L1(b), the live-app version, is bd-01M15R7D8VSTNW1XTSER2RRC25 and the hold on its app-versus-compiler placement assertion IS LIFTED: the parity fix landed at 04fdf6b, so the two surfaces now agree and that assertion tests something stable.

NOTE FOR THE OWNER: this landed in a repository that still has NO GIT REMOTE. The suite now exists only on this machine.
